newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.

text.p: For the week of Oct. 21, here are some of the top stories reported in major U.S. technology trade publications.

PC WEEK - Microsoft Corp's pricing strategies may erupt in a customer backlash as some information technology managers read the fine print on changes in their volume purchase programs, which may lead to certain corporate customers paying on average 15 percent more, PC Week reported in its Oct. 21 issue.

Compaq Computer Corp is struggling to meet demand for most of the models of its newest notebook computers in its Armada and LTE 5000 lines and it is also preparing to phase out a slew of older models, sources told PC Week.

COMPUTERWORLD - Tandem Computer Inc is expected to unveil next Wednesday a new server that will run Microsoft Corp's Windows NT operating system, the latest of proprietary computer system developers to adopt NT software, Computerworld reported in its Oct. 21 issue.

IBM's Lotus Notes users give the company low marks for sales and support, but they approve of Notes' quality and its Internet-based direction, according to a survey done by Computerworld of 152 IBM system shops.
